title: Does the Defect Travel with the Cell?

scenes.tts: How do you work out where a neuron came from, and what it needs for the trip? There are three ways to ask.
scenes.visual: Title card: Does the Defect Travel with the Cell? Three icons: an eye, a pair of scissors, two swapping arrows.
scenes.narration: How do you work out where a neuron came from, and what it needs for the trip? There are three ways to ask.

scenes.tts: Follow the cells out. Remove the source. Or swap tissue, and see which one the defect follows.
scenes.visual: Labels under the icons: follow, remove, swap.
scenes.narration: Follow the cells out. Remove the source. Or swap tissue, and see which one the defect follows.

scenes.tts: First, follow. In nineteen ninety-six, dye placed in the lateral eminence of cultured rat embryos marked cells that reached the cortex.
scenes.caption: First, follow. In 1996, dye placed in the lateral eminence of cultured rat embryos marked cells that reached the cortex.
scenes.visual: A dye spot in the lateral eminence. Labelled cells stream up into the side of the cortex. Credit: de Carlos, López-Mascaraque and Valverde, 1996.
scenes.narration: First, follow. In 1996, dye placed in the lateral eminence of cultured rat embryos marked cells that reached the cortex.

scenes.tts: But dye fades, and it does not say what a cell becomes.
scenes.visual: The dye glow fades. Label: route, not identity.
scenes.narration: But dye fades, and it does not say what a cell becomes.

scenes.tts: A genetic label fixes that. Cells that switch on N K X two point one, mostly in the medial eminence, turn on a reporter.
scenes.visual: Cells in the medial eminence, and a few in the nearby preoptic area, turn on a bright reporter; their daughters stay bright as they divide.
scenes.caption: A genetic label fixes that. Cells that switch on Nkx2.1, mostly in the medial eminence, turn on a reporter.
scenes.narration: A genetic label fixes that. Cells that switch on Nkx2.1, mostly in the medial eminence, turn on a reporter.

scenes.tts: Every descendant keeps the reporter, even after the gene turns off.
scenes.visual: The source gene's label switches off; the reporter glow stays on in every daughter.
scenes.narration: Every descendant keeps the reporter, even after the gene turns off.

scenes.tts: In mature mouse cortex, many marked cells are inhibitory interneurons.
scenes.visual: Mature cortex with bright reporter cells, many of them magenta interneuron dots.
scenes.narration: In mature mouse cortex, many marked cells are inhibitory interneurons.

scenes.tts: Second, remove. In nineteen ninety-seven, Stewart Anderson, John Rubenstein and colleagues cut mouse cortex away from the ventral forebrain.
scenes.caption: Second, remove. In 1997, Stewart Anderson, John Rubenstein and colleagues cut mouse cortex away from the ventral forebrain.
scenes.visual: A scalpel line separates cortex from eminence in a dish. Credit: Anderson, Eisenstat, Shi and Rubenstein, 1997.
scenes.narration: Second, remove. In 1997, Stewart Anderson, John Rubenstein and colleagues cut mouse cortex away from the ventral forebrain.

scenes.tts: The isolated cortex ended up with fewer cells containing gabba.
scenes.caption: The isolated cortex ended up with fewer cells containing GABA.
scenes.visual: GABA-cell dots in the cut cortex thin out.
scenes.narration: The isolated cortex ended up with fewer cells containing GABA.

scenes.tts: They also used a knockout, a mouse with a gene disrupted in every cell.
scenes.visual: Definition card: knockout, a gene disrupted in every cell.
scenes.narration: They also used a knockout, a mouse with a gene disrupted in every cell.

scenes.tts: They disrupted both D L X one and D L X two. These genes encode transcription factors made in the subpallium.
scenes.caption: They disrupted both Dlx1 and Dlx2. These genes encode transcription factors made in the subpallium.
scenes.visual: Gene labels Dlx1 and Dlx2 light up in the subpallium, then are crossed out.
scenes.narration: They disrupted both Dlx1 and Dlx2. These genes encode transcription factors made in the subpallium.

scenes.tts: In the mutant cortex, which neurons go missing?
scenes.visual: Normal and Dlx1/2 mutant cortex side by side, the mutant's cells hidden behind a question mark.
scenes.narration: In the mutant cortex, which neurons go missing?

scenes.tts: The inhibitory ones. No migration from the ventral forebrain into the neocortex was detected, and few cells contained gabba.
scenes.caption: The inhibitory ones. No migration from the ventral forebrain into the neocortex was detected, and few cells contained GABA.
scenes.visual: The mutant cortex is revealed: magenta dots mostly missing.
scenes.narration: The inhibitory ones. No migration from the ventral forebrain into the neocortex was detected, and few cells contained GABA.

scenes.tts: The pyramidal neurons were still made. Their progenitors do not need these genes.
scenes.visual: Green triangles present in both cortices.
scenes.narration: The pyramidal neurons were still made. Their progenitors do not need these genes.

scenes.tts: But a knockout lacks the genes in every cell. Is the fault in the travellers, or in the road?
scenes.visual: A traveller dot on a road; both marked as mutant. Question mark over each.
scenes.narration: But a knockout lacks the genes in every cell. Is the fault in the travellers, or in the road?

scenes.tts: In two thousand one, the same group answered with grafts.
scenes.caption: In 2001, the same group answered with grafts.
scenes.visual: Credit: Anderson, Marín, Horn, Jennings and Rubenstein, 2001.
scenes.narration: In 2001, the same group answered with grafts.

scenes.tts: They placed labelled pieces of eminence into forebrain slices, crossing normal and mutant tissue both ways.
scenes.visual: A coloured eminence piece is dropped into a grey forebrain slice. A two-by-two grid appears: donor by host.
scenes.narration: They placed labelled pieces of eminence into forebrain slices, crossing normal and mutant tissue both ways.

scenes.tts: A normal piece in a mutant slice, or a mutant piece in a normal slice. Which fails to migrate?
scenes.visual: Grid rows: normal donor into mutant host; mutant donor into normal host. Both outcomes hidden.
scenes.narration: A normal piece in a mutant slice, or a mutant piece in a normal slice. Which fails to migrate?

scenes.tts: Normal cells migrated into the cortex of mutant slices.
scenes.visual: Row one fills: normal cells stream into the mutant cortex. Tick.
scenes.narration: Normal cells migrated into the cortex of mutant slices.

scenes.tts: Mutant cells failed to migrate into the cortex of normal slices.
scenes.visual: Row two fills: mutant cells stay in the graft. Cross.
scenes.narration: Mutant cells failed to migrate into the cortex of normal slices.

scenes.tts: The defect travelled with the cells.
scenes.visual: Caption on screen: the defect travelled with the cells.
scenes.narration: The defect travelled with the cells.

scenes.tts: So whatever these genes do for the trip, they do it inside the travelling cells.
scenes.visual: A highlight moves from the slice to the travelling dot.
scenes.narration: So whatever these genes do for the trip, they do it inside the travelling cells.

scenes.tts: The swap shows where the need lies, not how the genes act.
scenes.visual: Two labels: where, answered; how, open.
scenes.narration: The swap shows where the need lies, not how the genes act.

scenes.tts: For D L X, the swap gives a clear answer. The defect travels with the cell.
scenes.visual: Closing card: for Dlx, the defect travels with the cell. Rule badge in the corner.
scenes.caption: For Dlx, the swap gives a clear answer. The defect travels with the cell.
scenes.narration: For Dlx, the swap gives a clear answer. The defect travels with the cell.
